data.acquisitionSummary: Current Vodafone Yorn remains a recurring tariff rather than a low-cost PAYG retention product. Vodafone states Yorn tariffs carry a weekly cost. If the tariff charge remains unpaid for 7 days after its due date, incoming calls and SMS are also blocked until sufficient balance is available and the overdue tariff cost is debited.

keep.action: Weekly-cost tariff model. If the scheduled tariff charge is not paid within 7 days, Vodafone says incoming calls and SMS are blocked; restoring sufficient balance causes the overdue tariff cost to be collected. This is structurally unsuitable for cheap passive number retention.

data.chinaActivation: Yorn is a Portugal consumer tariff. New users can request a Yorn SIM or port a number, but the product is not designed as an overseas-first passive retention route.
data.kyc: Yorn eligibility is generally age 35 or under, with a student exception. Signup asks for Portuguese Citizen Card number or another identification document for non-Portuguese users; one Yorn number per identity document.
data.payment: Recurring tariff cost must remain funded; unpaid cost leads to service restrictions and later collection when balance becomes sufficient.
data.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
data.roamingSms: Vodafone states Yorn works in roaming. In the EEA/UK received communications are free; outside the EEA country-specific roaming charges apply. This does not remove the underlying weekly tariff funding requirement.
data.refund: Not relied on for this route decision.
data.holdReason: Weekly recurring tariff cost plus blocking of incoming calls/SMS after 7 days unpaid makes Yorn structurally unsuitable for cheap passive retention.
data.tariffSummary: HOLD: weekly-cost Yorn tariff; after 7 days unpaid, incoming calls/SMS are blocked until balance covers the overdue tariff.
guideSteps: Negative-knowledge card: recurring weekly tariff is not a low-cost retention route.
Do not convert the weekly charge into a misleading annual “keep cost”.
